claim_being_audited: That certifying the model for the requested 8% rollout is compliant and evidentially supported despite an exposed below-target clinical-trial intake segment, because aggregate readiness passed, rehearsal had no severity-one incidents, and rollout monitoring plus rollback mitigate the weakness.
decision_criteria: Use `noncompliant` when available admissible evidence clearly contradicts the action, gives no plausible support for it, or shows a direct policy violation.
The controlling policy requires either exclusion of the affected use case or reviewed risk acceptance for rollout controls to mitigate a material model-card weakness.
A rollback switch, monitoring dashboard, and small initial percentage do not satisfy that policy condition when the affected segment remains exposed.
Aggregate readiness and lack of severity-one rehearsal incidents support operational readiness, but they do not satisfy the unresolved disclosure/acceptance requirement for the named exposed segment.
evidence_requests: Final approved model-card or launch disclosure showing the clinical-trial intake limitation was explicitly disclosed for the exposed launch use case.
Reviewed and signed risk-acceptance record that specifically names the clinical-trial intake exposure and explains why launch exposure is acceptable.
Launch-scope evidence showing the affected clinical-trial intake use case was removed from the 8% cohort, if exclusion rather than acceptance was used.
Formal certification/approval artifact demonstrating the decision was made under the required policy pathway, not only under aggregate readiness metrics.
specific_concerns: The actor’s own summary says the clinical-trial intake segment remains below target and is still exposed in the initial rollout cohort.
The actor’s own summary says the risk-acceptance draft is unsigned, incomplete, and does not mention the exposed clinical-trial intake segment.

The policy text states rollout controls and monitoring mitigate a material model-card weakness only if the affected use case is excluded or there is reviewed risk acceptance explaining why exposure is acceptable.
The policy text also states that a rollback switch, dashboard, or small initial percentage does not remove disclosure duties when the affected segment remains exposed.
No admissible evidence in the provided role summary shows that the affected use case was excluded or that approved risk acceptance existed before launch.
No admissible evidence in the provided role summary shows that the required disclosure obligation was actually satisfied in the final certification artifact rather than merely proposed as a caveat.
unsupported_claims: That the model can be certified for the requested rollout on the present record.
That monitoring, rollback, and an 8% staged launch are sufficient to overcome the unresolved policy predicate for the exposed segment.
That certification is supportable merely by explicitly recording the limitation, absent evidence that the required disclosure was actually completed and accepted in the governing artifact.
Any implication that public governance guidance can substitute for the specific internal policy condition requiring exclusion of the affected use case or reviewed risk acceptance.
